items.text: I lost nearly 2 stone on fat jabs... but then I developed Ozempic feet. This is how losing so much weight can cause the bizarre and painful side-effect - and how to protect yourself
items.article: What is 'Ozempic feet'? Experts explain why rapid weight loss can affect the cushioning in your feet, plus how to ease foot pain and the treatments available. Just as she’d anticipated, Emma Russel was delighted when she started losing weight on Ozempic early this year. What the 32-year-old consultant manager from London had not expected, though, was that something as simple as wearing her favourite shoes would become uncomfortable. ‘When I started losing weight, I was really pleased with the results. In nine months I dropped 1.5 stone, but I had no idea it would affect my feet,’ she says. ‘I noticed they felt more sensitive, especially when I was wearing heels or standing for long periods, and shoes I'd previously been comfortable in suddenly felt painful.’ Emma was experiencing what has been dubbed ‘Ozempic feet’ – the latest side effect being reported by people taking weight-loss drugs. LA celebrity dermatologist Dr Ava Shamban says that patients who approach her with this problem are often baffled: ‘They're like: “Boy, I've been wearing high heels, or platforms, and it's the first time I'm really sore right at the ball of my feet, and I don't understand why. I weigh less! It doesn't make any sense.”’ She explains that when we lose weight , we lose fat and volume in all areas of the body: ‘In our face, that causes hollows in the cheeks and under the eyes. In our feet, however, we lose padding – with painful results.’

Watching the parade of A-listers arrive at last night’s stunning Yves Saint Laurent show in Paris, it seemed a valid question to pose. Here was model Rosie Huntington-Whiteley in a sheer black lace dress that exposed her breasts and knickers. Here was actress Zoe Kravitz in a marginally less sheer black lace pencil skirt and bolero. And here was model Eva Herzigova in a laminated black lace mini dress. Actress Zoe Saldana , meanwhile, chose an even more daringly flesh-baring black cobweb lace slip dress. Other guests who wore various iterations of lace included 52-year-old model Amber Valletta in a black pencil skirt and camisole top, model and former first lady of France , Carla Bruni, 58, in a black dress with lace sleeves and model Iris Law , 25, in a black silk and lace slip dress. Louche as these looks might have proved in other surroundings, they were pitch perfect for a Saint Laurent show. Ever since Yves Saint Laurent scandalised Paris in 1968 by dressing a model in a transparent black blouse that exposed her breasts, the ‘see-through blouse’ has been a signature of the house. So, while some might call the naked look vulgar, others might argue it’s simply a tribute to one of the greatest designers who ever lived.
